title: Jus de Bouye, Baobab Fruit Juice
localName: Jus de bouye / pain de singe
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik)
desc: Baobab fruit soaked in a litre of boiling water, a litre of cold water added, worked by hand until it dissolves, picked of black seeds, sieved, then beaten with sugar and concentrated milk until the juice is ‘onctueux et homogène’.
longDesc: Amina Savoura’s jus de bouye, published on Afrik on 17 June 2017, uses 1/2 kg of bouye (also known as pain de singe or baobab fruit), 2 litres of water, 300 g of sugar, 3 packets of vanilla sugar and one can of concentrated milk — ‘sweetened or not’. The bouye is soaked in 1 litre of boiling water and 1 litre of cold water added; a few minutes later the baobab pulp dissolves as it is worked with the hands; the black seeds are removed; the pulp juice is sieved to remove impurities; the sugar is beaten in with a spatula, and the concentrated milk poured in in the same rhythm and well stirred. The page notes that a ‘royal’ version adds small pieces of pineapple, finely grated coconut and banana nectar. TWO GAPS: the page does not give the volume of the can of milk and does not choose between sweetened and unsweetened — and the choice materially changes the result. The vanilla sugar is listed in the ingredients but not placed in the method.
ingredients: 1/2 kg bouye (pain de singe, baobab fruit)
1 can concentrated liquid milk, sweetened or not — volume not printed and the choice is not made
2 litres water (1 L boiling plus 1 L cold, as in the method)
steps: Soak the baobab fruit in 1 litre of boiling water and add 1 litre of cold water.
A few minutes later the baobab will dissolve as you work it with your hands. Remove the black seeds, which carry no pulp.
Sieve the pulp juice through a fine sieve to remove impurities.

With a spatula, beat the juice rhythmically while adding the sugar and stirring. Keeping the same rhythm, pour in the concentrated milk and stir well. The page does not say where the vanilla sugar goes.
You should get a juice that is smooth, homogeneous and without imperfection.
chefTips: Two printed cues: the pulp dissolves as you work it by hand; the finished juice should be ‘onctueux et homogène sans imperfection’.
The only time printed is ‘quelques minutes’ after soaking.
Chilling is not mentioned on the page.
commonMistakes: Pouring the milk in without keeping up the stirring.
Leaving black seeds or fibre in.
Choosing sweetened condensed milk without cutting the 300 g of sugar — the page does not decide for you.
healthBenefits: Baobab is rich in vitamin C and fibre.
culturalNote: ‘Jus de Bouye royal’ is the variant with pineapple, grated coconut and banana nectar; no quantities are printed for it. A second page by Aïssatou Mbaye (4 September 2024) gives a lighter bouye juice for children but prints no quantities at all.
sources: Title as printed: «Le jus de Bouye». Byline as printed: «Amina Savoura», Afrik (afrik.com). «Publié le 17 juin 2017 à 21h25». Yield: none printed (8 used for scheduling). TWO-PASS, identical both passes including typos («1litre», «boite», «râpé»), not corrected.

ABSENT, not estimated: the volume of the can of milk; sweetened or unsweetened; where the 3 packets of vanilla sugar enter the method; the chilling. Time: «Quelques minutes après» is the only time printed; 5 minutes and 20 minutes prep above are scheduling estimates.
Arithmetic as printed: 2 litres of water in the list = 1 L boiling + 1 litre cold in the method — consistent.
